title: Normality and divisorial description of a log regular structure
statement: Let $(Y,N,\alpha)$ be a locally Noetherian log regular fs log scheme [def-trf-fs-log-blowup, pqf-def-locnoeth]. Let $V$ be the locus where the characteristic monoid $N/\mathcal O_Y^\times$ is zero, and write $j:V\hookrightarrow Y$. Then $V$ is open dense, every local ring of $Y$ is a normal domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], and the structural map identifies $N$ with the subsheaf $\mathcal O_Y\cap j_*\mathcal O_V^\times$ of the multiplicative sheaf $\mathcal O_Y$. In particular every section of $N$ restricts to a unit on $V$. On an integral affine open $\operatorname{Spec}C\subset Y$, $C$ is integrally closed in its fraction field.

source.place: Expose VI, 1.4, printed p. 69 (dense triviality locus and divisorial equality); Expose VIII, 3.4.1, printed p. 110, and 3.5, printed pp. 114--115 (fs log regular schemes are normal).

proof.text: Fix $\bar y$ over $y$ and put $A_0=\mathcal O_{Y,y}$, $A=\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{Y,\bar y}$. Choose a sharp chart $P\to N|_W$ and replace it on an affine pointed etale neighbourhood as allowed by the completed-chart lemma. Thus $\widehat A$ has one of its two displayed saturated monoid models, compatibly with the chart monomials. Apply the completed-monoid-chart normality criterion: $A_0$, $A$ and $\widehat A$ are normal domains and both canonical maps are faithfully flat. In particular every ordinary local ring of $Y$ is a normal domain.

source.place: VI 1.6; original steps 1--2 now use the separate completed-local normality criterion.

proof.text: At every geometric point, monoidal-ideal contraction supplies precisely the contraction hypothesis of the sharp-chart criterion, and step 1 supplies its domain hypothesis. Apply that criterion to these charts: $V$ is open dense, the structural maps on geometric stalks are injective, and log sections restrict to units on $V$. For generators $p_i$ the same criterion identifies $V\times_Y W=D(s_W)$ and its strict-local pullback with $D(s)$, where $s=\prod_i a(p_i)\neq0$.

source.place: VI 1.4 and VIII 3.4.3; original steps 3--4 now use the chart criterion.

proof.text: Let $f$ represent a germ of the divisorial sheaf at $\bar y$ on a pointed etale neighbourhood, and refine with $W$. Pulling its inverse back from $V$ to $D(s)$ makes $f$ a unit in $A[1/s]$. Apply faithfully flat monomial-unit descent with $B=\widehat A$: step 1 gives faithful flatness and the compatible model, and the complete-toric monomial-factor lemma gives its factorization hypothesis. Thus $f=u a(p)$ in $A$ with $u\in A^\times$. The chart formula $N_{\bar y}=P\oplus A^\times$ lifts $f$ to $N_{\bar y}$. The divisorial functions form a sheaf by gluing functions and their inverses; step 2 factors the structural map through it and gives stalkwise injectivity. The lifts just constructed give stalkwise surjectivity. Geometric-stalk detection identifies the two sheaves, compatibly with their multiplicative structures and structural maps.

source.place: VI 1.4, using VI 1.6; original steps 5--6 now use the separate algebraic descent criterion and elementary sheaf gluing.

proof.text: On an integral affine open $\operatorname{Spec}C\subseteq Y$, each maximal localization $C_{\mathfrak m}$ is an ordinary local ring of $Y$, hence a normal domain by step 1. The local-normality criterion makes $C$ integrally closed in its fraction field.

source.place: Affine-local consequence; Stacks Tag 030B, lemma-normality-is-local; original step 7 retained.

lean.statement: theorem logRegular_divisorialStructure (X : FineSaturatedLogScheme.{u}) (hX : X.IsLogRegular) : (∃ U : X.scheme.Opens, Dense (U : Set X.scheme) ∧ X.logStructure.trivialityLocus = (U : Set X.scheme) ∧ Presheaf.IsSheaf X.scheme.smallEtaleTopology (divisorialLogPresheaf U.ι) ∧ ∃ (e : X.logStructure.monoidSheaf.obj ≅ divisorialLogPresheaf U.ι), e.hom ≫ divisorialStructuralMap U.ι = X.logStructure.alpha ∧ ∀ (W : X.scheme.Etale) (s : X.logStructure.monoidSheaf.obj.obj (op W)), IsUnit ((pullback.fst W.hom U.ι).appTop (X.logStructure.alpha.app (op W) s))) ∧ (∀ y : X.scheme, IsDomain (X.scheme.presheaf.stalk y) ∧ IsIntegrallyClosed (X.scheme.presheaf.stalk y)) ∧ (∀ (U : X.scheme.Opens), IsAffineOpen U → IsIntegral U.toScheme → IsIntegrallyClosed (Γ(X.scheme, U)))
